The moist monsoonal flow continues to bring heavier showers and
isolated thunderstorms across the Marianas, especially for Tinian and
Saipan tonight. As newly formed Invest 91W develops and shifts
northeast, the monsoon flow will drift north with it by tomorrow. 
Drier air is then expected to move into the Marianas and lower 
precipitation chances through Saturday, especially for Guam and Rota.
By Sunday, monsoonal moisture may return to bring more scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms through early next week.

Marine...
Moderate to strong westerlies prevail across the Marianas,
gradually decreasing to gentle to fresh in the second half of the
week. Significant west swell, northerly swells and large 
localized wind waves are producing combined seas of 7 to 10 feet, 
maintaining hazardous conditions to small craft across Tinian and 
Saipan waters through at least Thursday afternoon. Sea conditions
look to remain just below levels hazardous to small craft through
the end of the week for Guam and Rota. There is a high risk of rip 
currents along west and north facing reefs through Thursday 
afternoon, potentially dropping below hazardous levels by tomorrow 
along north-facing reefs. A moderate risk of rip currents continues 
south facing reefs over the next few days. Scattered showers are 
expected tonight with isolated thunderstorms lasting through 
Wednesday night. Locally heavy showers are possible for Tinian and 
Saipan tonight.

Tropical Systems...
At 1:00 pm, Tropical Storm Peilou was centered well northeast of 
Saipan, and well west-northwest of Wake Island, near 25.1N 156.5E, 
moving NE at 29 mph. Peilou is now north of the Guam Area of
Responsibility (AOR). Peilou weakened to a TD overnight, but 
strengthened again to TS this morning, with maximum sustained winds 
of 40 mph. Peilou is expected to maintain this intensity through this
evening, then begin to weaken as it moves rapidly northeast.

For more information on TS Peilou, please see bulletins issued by 
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW
and by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

A broad, weak circulation, Invest 90W, is found NNW of Kwajalein, 
centered near 11.5N 167.1E, moving slowly west. A relatively cloud 
free Low-Level Circulation Center (LLCC) is seen on visible satellite
imagery. Invest 90W is currently rated sub-low, meaning it is not 
expected to become a significant tropical cyclone over the next few 
days. 90W is expected to continue moving slowly west over the next 
few days with little to no change in intensity.

Another weak circulation, Invest 91W, is centered near 22.2N 136.6E,
moving slowly eastward. Invest 91W is currently rated low, meaning
development is unlikely within the next 24 hours. Latest satellite
data indicates an elongated trough with convection seen along the
southern periphery of 91W. 91W is in a favorable area for
development, with low vertical wind shear, good outflow aloft and
warm sea surface temperatures. Model consensus on short term
development of a LLCC within the next 24 hours. Invest 91W will
continue to be monitored as it moves ENE over the next couple of
days.

For more information on Invest 91W, please see bulletins issued by 
JTWC under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A fairly dry pattern has moved into the Marshall Islands as Invest
90W slowly drifts west. 90W doesn't look like it will develop into
anything over the next several days, so it looks like the Marshalls
will remain dry through the weekend. Therefore, POPs (Probability of
Precipitation) were reduced to around 20 percent for Majuro through 
next Sunday. 

For Pohnpei and Kosrae, the main change in the forecast was to 
reduce POPs a bit. Numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms are 
still expected to continue through tonight, with POPs decreasing to 
the 30 to 50 percent range, or scattered, for the remainder of the 
week and the weekend. The main weather producers for tonight are a 
series of weak troughs interacting with some upper-level divergence. 
As the troughs move east and the divergence moves west, convection 
will decrease. However, influence from weak Invest 90W will help 
maintain POPs in the 30 to 50 percent range through the weekend.

Strong southeast to south winds in the southern hemisphere will
maintain a south swell of around 6 feet into Kosrae. This looks to
continue for a bit longer than previously expected, so decided to
extend the High Surf Advisory through 3 AM Thursday morning. Benign
conditions look to continue for Majuro and Pohnpei.
